A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FoREST study. All 24 pages of v2 and 27 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, tables, figures, and prompt specifications.

before.justification: v2 reports original QA, text-to-image, FoR identification, and human-study results, alongside diagnostic analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds spatial-configuration diagnostics and reversed-question-template evaluations.

M1.justification: The SG procedure still extracts direction, topology, distance, and FoR information before QA or layout generation. The prompting examples and layout instructions are unchanged. Appendix K.1 clarifies standalone FoR identification without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same English synthetic scenes, object categories, four FoR classes, and QA, text-to-image, and FoR identification tasks. Reversed questions preserve the underlying scenes and task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same models and prompting baselines. The o4-mini-high and human comparisons already appear in v2; their relocation in v3 does not add comparators. The new template experiment uses the existing Qwen2-72B prompting configurations.

E3.justification: v3 adds a separate evaluation using reversed locatum–relatum order across both splits and Qwen2-72B's four prompting settings (Appendix F.2). Appendix A.3 describes selecting normal and reversed templates for each scenario. The original temperature, few-shot, and diffusion-step settings remain.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds focused failure analyses stratified by facing direction and spatial-relation wording for Qwen2-72B and GPT-4o. Appendix F.2 adds question-order sensitivity testing. These extend the existing attention, template, temperature, layout, and qualitative analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged: both provide point estimates and individual and averaged human results. Neither introduces repeated-run uncertainty, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v3 adds diagnostic scores in Tables 10–11 and reversed-template results in Tables 13–14. For example, Table 10 reports Qwen2 zero-shot facing-direction averages of 57.87% for front and 10.50% for left. Retained numerical tables match. RQ2 also changes its GPT-4o summary from 72% to up to 82.4%, already present in v2 Table 2.

T1.justification: The FoR definitions and set-based task formulations retain their mathematical substance. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs; the added reasoning about model behavior is conceptual and empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: FoREST, evidence of FoR-dependent model weaknesses and biases, and SG prompting for QA and image-layout generation. Rewording does not materially change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: v3 extends the training-data explanation with hypotheses about overfitting particular facing directions and relation-specific extraction behavior (Appendix E). New RQ5 discusses human perspective-taking and model generalization, while Appendix F.2 interprets question-order effects. The English-only, synthetic-environment, and resource limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 and Table 7 document reversed templates and their generation and selection procedure; Appendix K.1 clarifies SG usage for classification. The explicit o4 reasoning-effort parameter statement is removed, although the high designation remains. Hardware, prompt examples, and code/data access are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds cognitive perspective-taking literature and discusses SPARTUN3D and Spatial457, further distinguishing FoREST from visual and situated spatial benchmarks. These extend the existing positioning. Bibliographic updates to retained works, such as the CoT reference, do not constitute new cited methods.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the introduction, dataset explanation, results discussion, and appendix prose are rewritten. Appendix sections are extensively reordered and renamed, terminology is standardized, and RQ5 is integrated into the main narrative. This exceeds localized copyediting.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn. v2's separate appendix dataset-statistics tables become a combined main-text Table 1. Tables throughout are extensively reformatted with revised rules, spacing, and headers; four diagnostic tables are added, and retained displays are relocated. Other result-figure content is preserved.

improvement.justification: The added diagnostics and question-order check strengthen the failure analysis, while the redesigned pipeline, clearer tables, and rewritten explanations improve readability. The gain is limited by overstatement: Section 3.4 says question order does not affect performance, yet v3 Tables 2 and 13 show A-split relatum-perspective SG+CoT accuracy of 86.2% with normal questions versus 78.9% with reversed questions.
